key_insight: Rice husk ash yielded amorphous SiO₂ after chemical treatment and heating at 800 °C for 3 h, then crystallized into quartz and cristobalite upon annealing at 1200 °C.
engineering_relevance: The resulting silica powders offer a potential agricultural-waste-derived feedstock for thermal spray coatings.
method: Chemically treat rice husk ash, then heat at 800 °C for 3 h.
Anneal at 1200 °C to produce crystalline silica phases.
Characterize structure, bonding, and particle size using XRD, FTIR, and laser diffraction.
evidence_signal: Characterization identified amorphous silica with D50 ≈ 88.9 µm, quartz and cristobalite after annealing, and Si–O–Si absorption bands at 1000–1100 cm⁻¹.
watch_item: The abstract reports powder characterization but no thermal spray trials or coating-performance validation.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
